title: Astrid and the Smile
premise: Wendell Amberdale has spent twenty years as a hospice nurse listening to the dying count backwards toward zero, and has kept his childhood imaginary friend, the Smile, safely locked in memory. When the Smile appears on his porch unchanged after forty years, Wendell learns it is a tether to something taken in 1974: his sister Astrid, who vanished that summer and was erased from every record and every mind but his. The Smile offers to return her — but the price is that Wendell must take her place in the placeless dark, and the countdown he hears in dying patients is his own. In the end, Wendell and Astrid refuse the bargain's terms, forcing the Smile to choose, and the creature that was invented out of a child's love finally learns what it means to be loved back — at the cost of its own existence.
about_author: Ivo Delacroix is the pen name of a former night-shift orderly who claims to have kept a ledger of every patient's last words. They write in a converted chapel in rural Vermont and refuse to be photographed.

chapters.title: The Counting Ward
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At Hollowmere Hospice, Wendell works his rounds as patients count backwards in their sleep — always stopping at different numbers. He keeps ritual tallies of lights and doors, and we learn his compulsions are armor against a childhood summer he cannot name. Emotional beat: dread dressed up as routine, and the loneliness of a man guarding a wound he can't locate.

chapters.title: Zero at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Patient Edith Marsh reaches zero and dies mid-count — but her last word is 'Astrid.' Wendell has never told anyone that name. He searches his own records and finds a gap: a sister-shaped hole in family photos, in his memory, in the hospice's oldest files. Emotional beat: the floor opening under a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: What the Porch Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Arriving home, Wendell finds the Smile waiting on his porch — unchanged since 1974, wide and patient. It speaks in his own childhood voice and tells him it has been counting too. It says: 'You kept her. Now give her back.' Emotional beat: terror braided with a horrible, homesick tenderness.

chapters.title: The Summer That Wasn't Filed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, with a flashback to 1974 in italics. Wendell digs through county archives and his mother's locked cedar chest, finding a coroner's report sealed by court order and a child's drawing of three figures: Wendell, the Smile, and a girl labeled only 'HER.' Emotional beat: the past pushing back against forty years of denial.

chapters.title: Terms of Return
chapters.summary: The Smile's POV, strange and childlike. The creature explains the rules: Astrid was taken as payment in 1974 when Wendell wished her away during a night of terror; she can be returned, but a life must fill the vacancy, and the countdown Wendell hears in the dying has been his own since the porch. Emotional beat: seduction — the Smile genuinely loves Wendell, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Nurse, Heal Thyself
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell tries to break the countdown by confessing to his supervisor, Father-figure colleague Rosa, and a therapist; each conversation unravels — Rosa hears him say a different name, the therapist's notes read 'no sister.' The Smile is editing the world around him. Emotional beat: gaslit isolation, the horror of unshared reality.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Interstitial
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Between places — a corridor of wallpaper and dusk — Astrid has been 'waiting' for fifty years without aging, sustained by the Smile's visits. She remembers her brother's face and the night she was traded. She has begun, quietly, to count too. Emotional beat: eerie calm over a slow-burning grief.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Oldest Resident
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell finds a patient no one admits to: Mr. Voss, 101, who was the county sheriff in 1974 and closed the case. Dying, Voss confesses that Astrid's death was staged — she was taken by the thing the town fed for generations, and the town's founding families knew. Emotional beat: justice deferred becoming justice demanded.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell and Rosa's POV alternating. Following Voss's clues, they find a ledger in the hospice's basement — Hollowmere was built on the site of the old offering ground. Every generation, a child was 'taken' and the town prospered. The Smile is not Wendell's friend; it is the town's collector. Emotional beat: righteous fury — the horror has a human accomplice.

chapters.title: Rosa Counts Backwards
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Rosa, who helped him open the ledger, begins counting in her sleep. The Smile is collecting interest. Wendell realizes every ally he recruits becomes collateral, and the Smile appears to say, gently, that it is only balancing the book. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized; love as leverage.

chapters.title: Astrid Learns the Shape of the Door
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the interstitial, Astrid discovers the corridor has doors — one for each child taken across generations, all still 'waiting.' She begins opening them, waking the others, and the Smile's perfect dusk starts to flicker. Emotional beat: agency kindling in the darkest room; hope as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Wish, Replayed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, deep flashback. The full memory returns: 1974, the night of the storm, young Wendell hiding from his father's rage and wishing — with the Smile's help — that his sister would 'go somewhere it can't reach.' The Smile, made of a child's wish, obeyed. Emotional beat: devastating self-knowledge; the villain and the victim share a face.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Bargain on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell offers himself at the old covered bridge, where the ledger says the exchanges happen. The Smile is moved — and tempted — but explains it cannot take a volunteer; the debt is specific, and the town's founding families still hold the paper. Wendell learns who they are: the hospice's own board of directors. Emotional beat: the horror pivots from supernatural to institutional.

chapters.title: The Board of Directors
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell infiltrates the board's annual meeting and finds the current members renewing the arrangement — their prosperity, their hospital, their names on the ledger. They offer him a deal: Astrid stays, Rosa is released, and Wendell gets a promotion and silence. Emotional beat: cold institutional evil; the moment Wendell chooses justice over safety.

chapters.title: Evidence of the Vanished
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV, fighting the countdown. Rosa, a former journalist, builds the case Wendell can't: photos, Voss's sworn statement recorded on her phone, the ledger photographed. But the world keeps editing it — files blank, her editor doesn't know her. She mails copies to herself and hides the originals in a patient's coffin. Emotional beat: tenacity against erasure; justice as paperwork and prayer.

chapters.title: The Other Children
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid and the awakened taken children reach the corridor's final door — the one the Smile keeps locked, its own origin: it was the first child taken, in 1891, and it forgot its name. The Smile arrives and begs Astrid to stop, because if the door opens, it remembers everything, including what was done to it. Emotional beat: the monster revealed as the first victim.

chapters.title: What the Smile Forgot
chapters.summary: The Smile's POV. The door opens. The creature remembers being Elias Wren, seven years old, and the founding families' first bargain. Its 'love' for Wendell was the shape its stolen childhood took. It offers Wendell the truth: it can return Astrid and every child, but it will unmake itself — and something older, the thing beneath the ledger, the actual collector, will wake hungry. Emotional beat: pity and horror fused.

chapters.title: The Thing Beneath the Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The true collector surfaces through the hospice — patients all counting to zero at once, lights failing, doors uncounting themselves. It is faceless, patient, contractual. It offers Wendell the same deal the board took: one life, any life, and the town is spared. Rosa's count reaches single digits. Emotional beat: the clock running out; every option costs someone.

chapters.title: Astrid Walks Out
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid refuses to be returned as property. She leads the taken children through the unlocked doors into the collector's hall and confronts it with the one thing it cannot ledger: they were never given, they were taken — the contract is void. Her declaration cracks the corridor. Emotional beat: the climax of justice outside the law; a stolen girl voiding a century of stolen contracts.

chapters.title: The Exchange Undone
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the covered bridge, Wendell, Astrid, and the Smile stand before the collector. Wendell offers not a life but the wish itself — he un-wishes 1974, taking Astrid's hand and telling the Smile it was never his to command. The Smile, choosing love over existence, steps into the vacancy itself. Emotional beat: sacrifice, forgiveness, and the terrible beauty of a monster's redemption.

chapters.title: The Names Come Back
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The taken children return across town — fifty years of unsolved vanishings resolving in a single dawn. The board members begin counting backwards and do not stop. Rosa's count halts at one and reverses. Astrid, fifty years old in a seven-year-old's debt, wakes in Hollowmere's care as records rewrite themselves around her. Emotional beat: cathartic restitution; grief and joy in the same breath.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. Wendell keeps nursing at Hollowmere, but the patients no longer count — they say names instead, and sometimes the name is Elias. Astrid, grown fast into the years owed her, lives in the cottage next door; they learn each other like new books. On the porch, where the Smile once waited, Wendell leaves the porch light on anyway. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — love that outlasted duty, and a light kept on out of gratitude, not fear.
